messages:
anya.dev: quick q — noticed a couple of customers hitting odd behavior with the JS SDK when running in mixed runtimes (Cloudflare Workers + node:18 lambda). global fetch exists sometimes, sometimes not. we should standardize a strategy.

sam.bryant: agreed. current SDK tries to import undici on Node and use globalThis.fetch otherwise, but that breaks in some bundlers + edge environments.

mohit.k: exact failures? stack traces?

anya.dev: stack is mostly: "TypeError: globalThis.fetch is not a function" in our retry wrapper. also some TS consumers report Response/Request types mismatch when they use undici types vs DOM lib.

sam.bryant: my proposal: (1) runtime detection utility that prefers native globalThis.fetch if it's a real WHATWG Fetch impl, (2) fallback to dynamic import('undici') only in Node-ish environments, (3) never ship node-only polyfills into bundles for edge runtimes.

anya.dev: that sounds right. how do we reliably detect a "real" fetch? typeof check sometimes isn't enough (polyfills faking it).

mohit.k: heuristic: check typeof globalThis.fetch === 'function' && typeof Response !== 'undefined' && Response.prototype && typeof Response.prototype.text === 'function'. Workers/Browser/Deno/Bun should pass. undici Response currently has a different prototype chain but still should pass basic checks. fallback if checks fail.

sam.bryant: also check for globalThis.Request and AbortController. if any are missing, treat as partial and prefer a controlled undici import in Node.

kevin_ops: what about Bun? Bun has a faster native fetch but also exposes Bun-specific globals. our detection should prefer Bun global, definitely avoid importing undici there.

anya.dev: +1. we should add a tiny doc table: preferred fetch source by runtime (browser/worker/deno/bun -> global, node <=18 -> undici polyfill optional, node 18+ -> global if present but watch for partial impls).

mohit.k: on the TS side: undici's types are not identical to lib.dom. that causes compile-time friction when downstream projects enable "dom" in tsconfig. suggestion: in our SDK types declare fetch types in terms of lib.dom (RequestInfo, RequestInit, Response) and in runtime picks the compatible implementation. basically, don't import undici types into our public declarations.

sam.bryant: yep. keep public typings DOM-based. internal runtime loader can import undici dynamically (no exported types). add a note in changelog about consumers who import undici types directly.

anya.dev: auth/retry implication: our retry wrapper wraps fetch and retries on 401 after refresh flow. if we dynamically choose fetch impls, we must ensure the wrapper preserves Request cloning semantics and body streams. undici Request bodies are different. any gotchas?

mohit.k: important: avoid passing a streamed body into retriable requests unless we can recreate it. solutions: (a) buffer small bodies (<=64k) for retries, (b) document that streaming bodies are non-retriable, (c) provide an opt-in 'cloneableBody' helper that users can use in advanced flows.

sam.bryant: implement a FetchAdapter interface in SDK: { fetch: typeof fetch, isCloneableBody(body): boolean, cloneBody(body): Promise<BodyLike> } and adapt per runtime. keeps retry code generic.

taylor_p: I can prototype the adapter and runtime detection util. plan: add tests for node18 (global), node16 (no global -> undici), cloudflare worker (global), bun (global). will also add a small sample app in examples/ that demonstrates correct bundler config for webpack/rollup/esbuild.

anya.dev: sample code we should show in README:
```js
// runtime-fetch.ts (usage in SDK internals)
export async function getFetch() {
  if (typeof globalThis.fetch === 'function' && typeof globalThis.Response !== 'undefined' && typeof globalThis.Request !== 'undefined') {
    return { fetch: globalThis.fetch }; // prefer native
  }
  // node fallback
  const { fetch } = await import('undici');
  return { fetch };
}
```

sam.bryant: add guard for environments that have a "fake" fetch (e.g., some test runners). also ensure bundlers don't inline import('undici') into browser builds. dynamic import should be preserved.

kevin_ops: CI concern — we need to run our unit tests across multiple runtimes to catch regressions. can we add a small matrix to GH actions: node16, node18, bun (latest), deno (latest), and a worker-like smoke test via Miniflare?

ci-bot: GH actions matrix updated: added node16,node18,bun-minor,deno, miniflare. Lint: OK, Tests: queued. :rocket:

mohit.k: action items: @taylor_p create PR with runtime-detection util + FetchAdapter interface; @anya.dev write README polyfill guidance and example for bundlers; @sam.bryant add unit tests for retry semantics and cloneable body cases; @kevin_ops add GH matrix entries.

anya.dev: thanks — let's aim to land this before the next minor. UX note: docs should include a short checklist for integrators: tsconfig (dom lib), bundler externals (don't bundle undici for browser), and how to handle serverless images that lack global fetch.

sam.bryant: one more: log a debug-level message when we fall back to undici so ops can triage mismatched runtimes.

kevin_ops: agreed. add telemetry event "runtime_fetch_selected" with label {source: 'global'|'undici'|'custom'} but scrub URLs/tokens.

anya.dev: perfect. good thread. I'll create a RFC doc with samples after the PRs land. :+1:
